clue.text: Attack from the right, for example, on minor highway

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a B-road is a British minor road, below an A-road
the right is one side, as of a road or a body

explanation.surface: A motorist is attacked from the right while driving along a country road.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a forceful verbal or naval assault, originally a volley from all guns on one flank of a ship.

clue.text: The Seine perhaps covers one area of France!

definitions.text: The Seine perhaps covers one area of France!

indicators.note: one piece lies over and around the other, so the river encloses the next word

parts.note: the Seine is an example of a river
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the Seine stretches over a whole region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a loose description of the answer, a coastal region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coastal strip of south-east France, the Côte d'Azur.

clue.text: Interpret bad sign in the gut

indicators.note: to interpret is to make something new of the letters, so the word bad is rearranged

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A soothsayer reads a bad portent in the entrails.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the abdominal region, where the gut lies.

clue.text: Individuals concealing temperature might wear them!

definitions.text: Individuals concealing temperature might wear them!

indicators.note: one word hides another inside it here, keeping the abbreviation out of sight

parts.note: single people are singles

explanation.surface: People hiding a fever might be wearing these garments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also a playful description: these sleeveless vests are worn by individuals.
explanation.definitionFit: Singlets are sleeveless vests, worn by athletes or as underwear.

clue.text: Land belonging to English nation?

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A question about whether a plot of land belongs to the English people.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of property in the country.

clue.text: The sort of tree always found on part of golf course

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
the green is the putting area of a golf hole

explanation.surface: A golf course with a particular kind of tree always beside the putting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree that keeps its leaves all year round, like a pine or holly.

clue.text: Farmer and rebel leader arrested by policeman

indicators.note: the policeman holds the letter inside himself, as if arresting it

parts.note: copper is British slang for a police officer

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of rebel

explanation.surface: A farmer and an insurgent chief are both taken into custody by a constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropper is a grower of crops, especially a sharecropping farmer.

clue.text: The sort of weapon that discharges thin gloss

indicators.note: to discharge is to let something fly out, so the words thin gloss are scattered and remade

explanation.surface: A weapon that fires off a thin glossy coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult made of a forked stick and elastic, a child's missile launcher.

clue.text: How many school leavers?

parts.note: a question about the number leaving school each year, answered vaguely with a word meaning some, more than two

explanation.definitionFit: The answer means more than two but not many, a vague reply to a question asking for a count.

clue.text: Clear identification needed in the case of something happening

indicators.note: a case is a container, so the abbreviation goes inside the occurrence

parts.note: an event is something that happens

explanation.surface: Proof of identity is required whenever an incident occurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious, plain to see, as in an evident mistake.

clue.text: Means of travelling first-class return, originally

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the digit 1 read as I

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning letter of the word return

explanation.surface: A traveller buys a first-class return ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying by aeroplane is one way to travel, as in going by air.

clue.text: Long for short number to remember

indicators.note: a short word has lost its final letter, cut off the end

parts.note: to pine for is to yearn or long for

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for a brief number that they must keep in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal identification number is the secret code memorised for bank cards.

clue.text: Sort of wine to spice — and in burgundy with fish

parts.note: red is a kind of wine
to mull wine is to heat it with spices
et is French for and, the language of Burgundy

explanation.surface: A recipe: spice some wine and serve it with fish in a burgundy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burgundy' looks like the wine but stands for the French region, so 'and' is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A red mullet is a reddish Mediterranean food fish.

clue.text: Description of article found in Yorkshire's last mine

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of Yorkshire is used
the article is placed within the mine, as if found down it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An item discovered down the last coal mine in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase attached to a name, like the Great in Alfred the Great.

clue.text: Noblewoman crossing line — it's unparalleled!

indicators.note: the noblewoman spans the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a peeress is a female peer

explanation.surface: A titled lady crosses a line, and the result is beyond compare.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no equal; without peer or match.

clue.text: Heartless aristocrat from the London area

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: a baronet is a hereditary titled aristocrat

explanation.surface: An unfeeling nobleman comes from a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is a borough of north London; in rhyming slang it also means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnet is a north London borough and its district.

clue.text: A definition of circulation given by old poet, perhaps?

definitions.text: A definition of circulation given by old poet, perhaps?

parts.words: A definition of circulation given by old poet, perhaps?
parts.note: the classification of what circulates in the veins: A, O and B (bard) read as letters standing for blood groups

explanation.definitionFit: A blood group classification such as A, B, AB or O.

clue.text: Duck under the covers?

parts.note: a bird's soft feathers end up beneath the bedclothes, as filling for a quilt

explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with the soft breast feathers of a sea duck.

clue.text: Atomic requirement that's protecting drunk before work

indicators.note: the outer letters shield the inner pieces by surrounding them

parts.note: i.e., Latin id est, means that is

indicators.note: one piece comes ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Something needed for the atom bomb shields a drunkard before he gets to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotope is a form of an element differing in neutron count, a requirement in atomic physics.

clue.text: Smoker depressed by silence

parts.note: a pipe is something smoked
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A gloomy smoker is upset by quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe down is to be quiet; the clue uses silence as a command, shut up.

clue.text: Supply vessel boarded by swimmer? No — the opposite!

indicators.note: boarding is getting inside, so one piece goes into the other
reverses the boarding: the swimmer takes the vessel in, not the other way round

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship is boarded by a swimmer, then the clue changes its mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish is to provide or equip with something.

clue.text: Introduce son, unable to move outside

indicators.note: the motionless word sits round the abbreviation

parts.note: inert means motionless

explanation.surface: Bringing in a son who cannot get out.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to put something in, to introduce it.

clue.text: Understood refusal, and very loudly got cut short

parts.note: saw means understood, as in I saw what he meant
no is a refusal
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone sees a no coming and shouts until cut off mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off shotgun has its barrel shortened.

clue.text: Soldiers dish out with modesty

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
to serve is to dish out food

explanation.surface: Soldiers hand out food in a modest manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve is restraint in manner, a reticence close to shyness.

clue.text: Steel cup on display — no way that's luxury

indicators.note: on display, the letters are set out in a fresh arrangement
no means the next abbreviation is taken away from the first word

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A steel cup is shown without a path, and the result is lavishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no way' removes ST from Steel, leaving EEL; EEL with CUPON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth and lavish display.

clue.text: One might run from joker, stifling a cry of pain

indicators.note: smothering, so the cry is held inside the joker

parts.note: a card is a joker, a comic person
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a prankster who is muffling a yelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward runs away from danger.

clue.text: Strange and knowing differently

parts.note: other can mean different or strange
wise means knowing

explanation.surface: Someone strange and wise thinks in a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: In another way, as in he thought otherwise.

clue.text: Can it be source of trouble at home?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A question whether a container could cause domestic strife.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can for food.

clue.text: Owing, we hear, for deposit in the morning

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: due means owing, as in money due

explanation.surface: A debt is said to be settled by a morning payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew is moisture that condenses on grass overnight.

clue.text: Strength on our side revealed rewards

indicators.note: the answer is uncovered within the run of words strength on our side

explanation.surface: Our team's power has been shown, earning prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Honours are awards, titles or distinctions given as a reward.

clue.text: Period during which there is competition for mail services

definitions.text: Period during which there is competition for mail services

parts.words: Period during which there is competition for mail services
parts.note: an era read as letters fighting conflict after the world wars, with conflict among mail firms as the cryptic reading

explanation.definitionFit: The time after a war, especially after the Second World War.

clue.text: Meant to replace leader with Democrat, being formal

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: signified means meant

explanation.surface: Something intended to substitute a party leader with a Democrat, done with solemnity.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignified means stately and serious in manner.
